newsitem.title: FRANCE: French police sue over Spanish death squad charges.
newsitem.headline: French police sue over Spanish death squad charges.

text.p: A state prosecutor asked a Paris court on Friday to fine the Madrid daily El Mundo for carrying allegations that a French police chief was bribed into helping Spanish death squads wage war on Basque refugees.

The policeman, Joel Cathala, is suing El Mundo for libel over allegations by a former Spanish Basque official who said he paid Cathala 1.5 million francs ($300,000) for intelligence on Basque separatist exiles.

The Spanish official, Angel Lopez Carrillo, said the documents were used by the Anti-terrorist Liberation Groups (GAL) to attack suspected ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) guerrillas in France in 1983-87.
He repeated his allegations in the Paris court, but was unable to describe precisely Cathala's office where he says he was handed cash on five occasions between 1984 and 1987.
Cathala, who at the time headed border police in the French Basque region, denied the allegations and recalled that his forces had detained several ETA leaders in the period when GAL was active.
ETA has killed hundreds of people in Spain in a campaign for a separate Basque state.
The French state prosecutor asked the court to fine two managers and three journalists of El Mundo. He did not request any specific amount. The court will rule at a later date.

Five of Cathala's former collaborators supported him in court, saying French police had no reason to help GAL. They said the death squads meant trouble for French police by causing unrest in the Basque region.
GAL killed 27 people in France in the 1980s, including several French nationals mistaken for ETA members.
GAL's dirty war has turned into a major scandal in Spain where a former interior minister and other top Socialists have been charged with funding the shadowy death squads.
